findings.evidence: Hosts restates that Claude Code and opencode read ~/.claude/skills, pi reads ${PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR:-~/.pi/agent}/skills, and Cursor reads ~/.claude/skills.
findings.fix: Drop the host skill-directory facts the harnesses already implement; keep only the documented Codex duplication gap and the 'not live-verified' flags.

findings.evidence: Threshold: the row's `min_confidence` is a conservative retained default; the live 32-case eval in this repo (see the eval object below); `JEV_MIN_CONFIDENCE` overrides it for one call.
findings.fix: Finish the sentence so the default is tied to the measured result: the 32-case eval proposed null, so min_confidence 0.7 stays, and JEV_MIN_CONFIDENCE overrides it for one call.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list gives reasons, but there is no Gotchas heading for the environment facts that defy assumptions (Laya state bleed, uncalibrated confidence, alias drift).
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas section that points at those three facts and their reasons, leaving the detail in reference.md.

findings.evidence: Description covers WHAT, WHEN and the not-for boundary, but omits the shorthand trigger words an agent matches on: ladder, probe, consent, needs_fallback is named only as a result, and evidence screening is not a keyword.
findings.fix: Use when a fast, cheap typed judgment beats a full reasoning pass: yes/no (noul), picking among named options (choice), a rubric score (score), or screening evidence against a criterion, through the shared System One client on Laya (local) or TypeSafe (remote, consent required), including ladder, probe and consent grant or revoke. Advisory only: needs_fallback means you decide that item yourself, and no answer is a verdict or gate. Not for building TypeSafe into an app (typesafe-ai) or for editing code.

findings.evidence: Key sources, in order: TYPESAFE_API_KEY, JEV_API_KEY, the first line of the file JEV_API_KEY_FILE names, a TYPESAFE_API_KEY= or JEV_API_KEY= line in secrets.env, then the first line of the state api_key.
findings.fix: Copy the order from scripts/jev_review.py _typesafe_key: env names, then the whole first non-empty line of JEV_API_KEY_FILE, then a secrets.env assignment, then the state file's first non-empty line, and last a ~/.mycreds assignment. Say the state file is not assignment-parsed.

findings.evidence: The TYPESAFE_API_KEY cell lists six sources in one row, including a transitional ~/.mycreds path, while backends/typesafe.md stops at the state file.
findings.fix: Keep one ordered default in backends/typesafe.md and make the environment table point at that list instead of restating a longer order.

findings.evidence: The casual-flaky-ci assertion requires an item of type noul that has an id, instructions and context, while the prompt supplies a CI summary to screen against a criterion, which the skill's own shorthand shape is {id, criterion, evidence}.
findings.fix: Split the assertion so a shorthand screen item (id, criterion, evidence) and a noul item (id, type, instructions, context) are both acceptable when the evidence stays value-free.

findings.evidence: eval_cases.py is a tracked script with structured JSON output, but its main() builds the parser with no --help text beyond argparse defaults, unlike jev_review.py.
findings.fix: Give eval_cases.py an ArgumentParser description and flag help that names --record and --calibrate, matching the module docstring.

findings.evidence: An agent that follows this file puts the key only in the state file's first line and never tries ~/.mycreds, while reference.md line 114 and _typesafe_key try ~/.mycreds last and read the state file as a raw first non-empty line, not an assignment.
findings.fix: State one key order, the one _typesafe_key implements, in backends/typesafe.md and point reference.md at it: env, JEV_API_KEY_FILE (whole first non-empty line), secrets.env assignment, state file (whole first non-empty line), ~/.mycreds assignment.
